name: Marder 1A3
characteristics: Strength: Well-proven Cold War IFV design, integrated ATGM gives organic anti-armor capability beyond the autocannon
Limitation: Aging design (1970s) relative to newer IFVs donated to Ukraine; aluminium armor lighter than modern composite types
Estimated quantity available: Donated in the dozens; exact current total not fully disclosed
employment_notes: One of the earliest Western IFVs delivered (2023), used to reinforce mechanized infantry as Soviet-legacy BMP stocks depleted
contrast_vs_traditional: Marder doctrine paired IFVs with tanks in a combined-arms breakthrough, using armor to protect dismounting infantry at the objective. On a front where a moving column is exactly what persistent drone ISR is built to find, getting infantry to a position increasingly means dismounting well short of it and moving the last stretch on foot under cover — the IFV's armor now protects the approach, not the arrival.
